Amazon OpenSearch Serverless is protected by AWS global network security. For information
about AWS security services and how AWS protects infrastructure, see AWS Cloud Security. To
design your AWS environment using the best practices for infrastructure security, see Infrastructure
Protection in Security Pillar AWS Well‐Architected Framework.
You use AWS published API calls to access Amazon OpenSearch Serverless through the network.
Clients must support Transport Layer Security (TLS). We require TLS 1.2 and recommend TLS 1.3.
For a list of supported ciphers for TLS 1.3, see TLS protocols and ciphers in the ELB documentation.

Additionally, you must sign requests using an access key ID and a secret access key that is
associated with an IAM principal. Or you can use the AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to
generate temporary security credentials to sign requests.
